newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end weak, Creative soars.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end weak, Creative soars.

text.p: Concerns over the U.S. March employment data, scheduled for release late in the day, weighed on the Singapore stock market on Friday, dealers said.
"If it shows higher than expected growth, the markets are going to tumble and fears of rate hikes, which have been plaguing markets, are going to be be reinforced," said a dealer.
Dealers said Malaysian central bank curbs on bank loans for property and share purchases continued to dampen trading with forced selling evident.

The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index ended 2.30 points lower at 2,075.78. UOB OTC index fell 6.29 points to end at 1,224.08. Turnover was over 170 million shares, with 220 losers against 132 gainers.
Multimedia Creative Technologies surged Singapore $3.30 to end at a high of S$16.90 after it said better earnings and margins were expected.

Debutante New Toyo, a maker of paper products, suffered from poor market sentiment and ended at its initial public offer price of S$0.80 after hitting a low of S$0.77. It topped the actives with over 7.1 million shares traded.
Dealers said banks and selected property counters continued to shine.
